seoTitle: Valencia cruise port guide: bus 4 to the old town, CAC
seoDescription: Valencia cruise port 2026: no walk to town. EMT bus 4 or 95 from Pont de les Drassanes, €2, about 45 min to the old town. Lonja €2, cathedral €10.
quickAnswer: Ships dock; Valencia is not a tender port, but the port is about 4.5 km from the old town, too far to walk comfortably. Walk about 10 minutes to the Pont de les Drassanes bus stop and take EMT bus 4 to the old town (about 45 minutes) or bus 95 to the City of Arts and Sciences (about 20 minutes), €2 a ride (2026). Because you depend on a bus or taxi, be back on board 90 minutes before all-aboard.
intro: Valencia gives you two cities in one call: the medieval old town around the cathedral, the Lonja and the Central Market, and the modern City of Arts and Sciences at the far end of the Turia gardens, a former riverbed turned park. Neither is close to the ship, so the day is about transport. Public buses are cheap but slow; taxis are quick; ship shuttles vary by line. There is no tourist tax and no cruise visitor cap in 2026, and the city beaches at El Cabanyal and Malvarrosa are the one thing you can reach on foot.

terminals.name: Trasmed passenger terminal (Moll de Ponent)
terminals.notes: In the south zone of the port, next to the Muelle de Poniente, at the port entrance closest to the city. Used for check-in and by ships under 300 m. Wheelchair accessible, with a bar, shops and free wifi. Taxis wait at the official rank by the door; ride-hailing pick-ups are in the outdoor area.

terminals.name: Cruise quays in the northern extension
terminals.notes: Ships over 300 m berth further out. A port shuttle links these quays with the Trasmed terminal, about 2–2.5 km away; you then leave the port on foot or by taxi from there.

walkability.detail: The old town is about 4.5 km and an hour on foot from the Trasmed terminal, along busy roads; take a bus or taxi. The Cabanyal and Malvarrosa beaches are the exception: 20–25 minutes on foot.

transportSections.mode: EMT bus 4 to the old town
transportSections.time: About 45 min to the Torres de Serranos area
transportSections.detail: From the 'Pont de les Drassanes – Terminal marítima' stop (no. 1306), about 10 minutes' walk from the terminal. Goes to the historic centre. Return from the stop on the opposite side of the road. Traffic can make it slower.

transportSections.time: About 20 min to the City of Arts and Sciences; about 15 min to La Marina–Neptú
transportSections.detail: Same stop as line 4. Runs along the Turia gardens and links the port, the City of Arts and Sciences and the old-town edge, so it suits a loop day.

transportSections.time: About 15 min to the centre once on board
transportSections.detail: Walk from the port to Marítim station and take line 5 or 7 towards the centre (Colón or Xàtiva). Faster than the bus once you reach the station.

transportSections.cost: Metered; check the fare before you go
transportSections.time: 15–20 min to the old town; 10–12 min to the City of Arts and Sciences
transportSections.detail: Official rank at the terminal door. Uber, Cabify and Bolt operate; pick-up in the terminal's outdoor area. For three or four people, often the quickest option.

transportSections.cost: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
transportSections.detail: Some lines sell a shuttle that drops near the Torres de Serranos or Plaza del Ayuntamiento. It is a ship service, not a port service, so it may not run on your call.

returnTiming.rule: Leave the old town by 15:30 for a 17:30 all-aboard (be on board by 16:00).
returnTiming.detail: Bus 4 takes about 45 minutes in traffic, plus the 10-minute walk from the Drassanes stop and terminal security. From the City of Arts and Sciences, bus 95 is about 20 minutes. If your ship is at the northern extension, add the port shuttle.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Take a taxi or a ride-hailing car: 15–20 minutes from the old town to the terminal. Call the port agent number in your daily programme if you will be late.

excursionAdvice: Valencia is easy on your own: two bus lines cover everything, and the cost is a few euros. A ship tour or shuttle is worth it if you want no transport planning at all, if you have mobility problems and do not want buses, or for trips outside the city such as the Albufera lagoon. For the old town and the City of Arts and Sciences, do it yourself.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes docking at the Trasmed terminal at 08:00 on a weekday (the Central Market is closed on Sundays).

steps.what: Walk 10 minutes to the Pont de les Drassanes stop and take EMT bus 4 to the historic centre (about 45 minutes).
Central Market: coffee and breakfast at a stall bar.
Lonja de la Seda, across the street (€2, about 45 minutes).
Walk to Plaza de la Virgen and the cathedral; visit with the audioguide (about 1 hour).
Lunch in the old town, then walk to the Torres de Serranos and the Turia gardens.
Bus 95 along the Turia to the City of Arts and Sciences (about 20 minutes). Walk around the buildings and pools, or visit the Science Museum.
Bus 95 back towards the port (about 20 minutes) and walk to the terminal.
Back on board, 90 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Valencia Cathedral
sights.why: Gothic cathedral with a chapel holding the agate cup venerated as the Holy Grail.
sights.tip: Tourist visits do not start until 14:00 on Sundays and holidays. Combine with the Basilica and Plaza de la Virgen next door.

sights.name: Lonja de la Seda (Silk Exchange)
sights.why: Late-Gothic merchants' hall with twisted columns, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
sights.cost: €2, €1 reduced; free on Sundays and holidays (2026)
sights.tip: Open 10:00–19:00 Monday to Saturday, 10:00–14:00 on Sundays and holidays. It faces the Central Market.

sights.name: Central Market (Mercado Central)
sights.why: Modernist market hall of iron, glass and tiles, still a working food market.
sights.tip: Open Monday to Saturday 07:30–15:00; closed Sundays and holidays. Go in the morning; ask before photographing stallholders.

sights.name: City of Arts and Sciences
sights.why: Santiago Calatrava's white buildings and pools at the end of the Turia gardens.
sights.cost: Free to walk around; Oceanogràfic, Science Museum and Hemisfèric combined €47.75 (2026)
sights.tip: The combined ticket can be spread over up to three days, which a cruise call cannot use; if you only have a few hours, pick one venue. Hemisfèric shows do not admit latecomers.

sights.name: Turia gardens
sights.why: A long park in the old riverbed, linking the old town with the City of Arts and Sciences.
sights.tip: Bus 95 runs alongside, so you can walk one section and ride the rest.

sights.name: Torres de Serranos
sights.why: The 14th-century city gate on the edge of the old town, overlooking the Turia gardens.
sights.tip: Bus 4 and many ship shuttles stop close by.

sights.name: El Cabanyal and Malvarrosa beaches
sights.why: Long, wide city beaches, the only sights within walking distance of the ship.
sights.tip: Walk 20–25 minutes from the terminal, or take bus 95 to La Marina–Neptú (about 15 minutes).

beaches.name: Las Arenas / El Cabanyal
beaches.howToGetThere: Walk from the terminal, or bus 95 to La Marina–Neptú
beaches.time: 20–25 min on foot; about 15 min by bus
beaches.note: Wide sandy beach with a promenade lined with paella restaurants.

beaches.name: Malvarrosa
beaches.howToGetThere: Continue north along the promenade from Las Arenas, or tram lines 4 and 6 to the beach stops
beaches.time: A further walk along the seafront
beaches.note: Quieter at the northern end; the promenade is flat.

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying to walk from the ship to the old town.
commonMistakes.fix: It is about 4.5 km on busy roads. Take bus 4, the metro from Marítim, or a taxi.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning the Central Market on a Sunday.
commonMistakes.fix: It is closed on Sundays and holidays and closes at 15:00 on other days. Go in the morning.

commonMistakes.mistake: Visiting the cathedral on a Sunday morning.
commonMistakes.fix: Tourist visits start at 14:00 on Sundays and holidays.

commonMistakes.mistake: Buying the three-venue City of Arts and Sciences ticket for a single port day.
commonMistakes.fix: It is designed for up to three days. Choose one venue, or just walk around the buildings for free.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaving the return to the last minute on bus 4.
commonMistakes.fix: Allow 45 minutes plus the walk, and be on board 90 minutes before all-aboard.

safety: Valencia is safe for day visitors. Pickpockets work the busiest spots: the Central Market, Plaza de la Reina, the cathedral square and crowded buses. Keep bags closed and in front. Watch for bikes and scooters on the Turia paths and the beach promenade. In summer, carry water; the City of Arts and Sciences has little shade.
scams: Pickpockets in the Central Market and around Plaza de la Reina, often working in pairs while you are distracted at a stall.
Card terminals and ATMs offering to charge in your home currency (dynamic currency conversion). Always choose euros.
Unofficial drivers approaching passengers outside the terminal. Use the official taxi rank at the terminal door or a ride-hailing app.
accessibility: The Trasmed terminal is wheelchair accessible. The old town and the Turia gardens are flat, and the Central Market, the Lonja's main hall and the cathedral are at street level. The cathedral bell tower (Micalet) has 207 steps and no lift. The City of Arts and Sciences is flat and spacious. Bus stops are a 10-minute walk from the terminal, so a taxi is often the easier choice for wheelchair users.
rainyDay: The Central Market, the Lonja and the cathedral cluster within a few minutes of each other and are all indoors. At the City of Arts and Sciences, the Science Museum, the Hemisfèric and the Oceanogràfic aquarium halls work well in rain.
crowdTips: Valencia has no cap on cruise passengers; the city says it manages arrivals by season rather than by a fixed number. Cruise passengers fell to about 768,000 in the year to May 2025. The Central Market is busiest late morning; arrive early. The cathedral and the Lonja are quieter on weekday mornings. On Sundays the Lonja is free and busy, the market is shut, and the cathedral opens only in the afternoon.

faqs.q: Is Valencia cruise port walkable to the city?
faqs.a: Not really. The old town is about 4.5 km away, an hour on foot along busy roads. The Cabanyal and Malvarrosa beaches are 20–25 minutes' walk.

faqs.q: How do I get from Valencia cruise port to the old town?
faqs.a: Walk about 10 minutes to the Pont de les Drassanes stop and take EMT bus 4 (€2, about 45 minutes), walk to Marítim for metro line 5 or 7, or take a taxi (15–20 minutes).

faqs.q: Is there a shuttle bus from Valencia cruise port?
faqs.a: A port shuttle links the outer cruise quays with the Trasmed terminal. Shuttles into the city are sold by some cruise lines and are not guaranteed, so check your cruise planner.
No. Ships dock, either at the Trasmed terminal on the Moll de Ponent or at the cruise quays in the northern extension.

faqs.q: Is there a tourist tax for cruise passengers in Valencia in 2026?
faqs.a: No. The Valencian tourist tax, which would have included cruise passengers, was repealed in 2023 before it took effect, and nothing applies in 2026.

faqs.q: What can I do in Valencia in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: The Central Market, the Lonja and the cathedral in the morning, then bus 95 along the Turia gardens to the City of Arts and Sciences, and back to the port on the same line.
Las Arenas, El Cabanyal and Malvarrosa are 20–25 minutes on foot from the terminal, or about 15 minutes on bus 95.

faqs.q: Is Valencia safe for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: Yes. Watch for pickpockets in the market and busy squares.
